raw_recipe.headline: Bob's Blue Cheese Dressing
raw_recipe.description: Bob's creamy blue cheese dressing recipe includes mayo, sour cream, hot pepper sauce, and honey. Serve over your favorite greens, or as a crudité dip.
raw_recipe.name: Bob's Blue Cheese Dressing

review.reviewBody: This is the best blue cheese dressing ~ and I love blue cheese! I only order blue cheese dressing on my salads, and have tried numerous recipes. This is is reminiscent of the restaurant that you went to and said " Wow, now THIS is good blue cheese!"

This turned out better than expected and used ingredients I already had on hand. I cut the recipe to just 1/4 of the volume. I also used reduced fat mayo, extra lemon juice, slightly less salt, gorgonzola vs standard blue cheese and added shallots. Blended it all up in my handheld food processor since it was a small amount. It turned out super creamy and very thick. It still yielded nearly a cup of dressing, which is more than enough IMO - I don't think it'd store super well for more than a couple of days. It'd be easy to make it into a dip as is or by adding a tad more cheese. I probably won't buy blue cheese dressing at the store now that I know how to whip this up.

This is an excellent blue cheese dressing! I've even made it with non-fat plain Greek yogurt replacing the sour cream and it's still delicious. I did add a couple Tablespoons of dry powdered buttermilk (for baking) to the yogurt variation but other than that left it the same. I think the buttermilk mix may help it stay thickened some too. So yummy!

I imagine that part of the secret to a blue cheese dressing recipe is starting with a blue cheese with an irresistibly good flavor, which I did. The brand of mayo may also be a factor in the success. I used Duke's Mayonnaise and was very happy with it. The equal parts of sour cream, mayo and blue cheese in this recipe are just right. Once I mixed these together, then added the lemon, it tasted exactly like what I was hoping the finished dressing would taste like, so I stopped there. I chilled it for a few hours and, to avoid watery dressing, waited to add the parsley until right before serving. Limiting this recipe to the base ingredients makes for a very simple dressing, but it was some of the best blue cheese dressing I've ever had. Others raved over it, too.

you MUST let it sit in the fridge for a bit. i made it and immediately put some in my salad and it was bleh lol but the next day it was like a completely different dressing, so so so good (not sure if you need to let it sit a whole day, but i did). we left out the Worcestershire sauce cause we didn't have enough to get it this week and it is still great so i wouldnt worry about it if you dont have it. we had it with iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, and trader joe's sausage cut up into bits and cooked first

My pantry was pretty bare. All I had to work with was mayo, sour cream, crumbled blue cheese, salt, and pepper. Good basic tasting creamy blue cheese dressing. I blended up the ingredients, except I reserved half the blue cheese to sprinkle on top of salad.

Tweaked this a little to lighten up the recipe.1/2 C Mayo & 1/2 C plain Greek yogurt. 3/4 Tbl. Dill flakes & 1 Tbl. Parsley flakes. Replaced hot sauce with chili powder-same measurement. WOW is this delicious.
My opinion this has too many flavors, I’d rather enjoy the blue cheese flavor a little more. Next time I’ll half the parsley, half the lemon juice and eliminate the hot sauce.
I just made this and substituted low fat plain greek yogurt since my boyfriend absolutely detests mayo. it was a hit with both of us on top of a huge vegetarian salad.

I made this dressing according to the recipe. Too, too salty (blue cheese is salty to begin with) and the honey gave it a rather odd sweet taste. I refridged for 1 hr thinking it may improve over time, but it just got saltier. I dumped it and remade omitting the honey, cutting down the salt to 1/2 tsp, pepper to 1/4 tsp and the Worcestershire to 1 tsp. Perfect

I substituted a lot...added real mustard, garlic salt instead of sea salt, apple cider vinegar instead of Worcestershire, avocado oil just because, 1/2 blue cheese & 1/2 feta cheese, spinach instead of parsley flakes, apple honey instead of regular. I liked this recipe but I think mine came out just as well!
Awesome can't wait to try😎👍👍
It's good and certainly better than anything you'll find off the shelf in the grocery store, but Bob's is still better. I'm going to keep looking. Next time I'll try one with buttermilk.

Stunning. Beats any store-bought dressing by a mile, and I believe it's cheaper. I chose this recipe over other 5-star contenders because it uses common ingredients--the other recipes called for small amounts of buttermilk. Who's gonna buy a quart of buttermilk to use just a little? Everything in this recipe is in your common pantry.

That is the Best Blue Cheese Dressing I have ever had. It was not a strong tast of blue cheese, I wanted to eat the whole bowl full. I made a salad and wanted some homemade blue cheese dressing to go with it. I am taking it to a sewing group tomorrow. I am taking 2 different dressing so that everyone can have a choice of there own dressing. I will be making it again.

Wow! I just made this and followed the recipe co a T. It is outstanding, restaurant grade. I always have trouble finding a clean dressing that has great flavor. This is it! I don’t think I’ll buy dressing again.

This is an excellent recipe for blue cheese dressing. It has a thick yet pourable consistency that clings nicely to salad. Each of the ingredients combine to create rich dimensions in the overall flavor. I wish every restaurant served blue cheese dressing as great as this!
This is , hands down, my favorite recipe for blue cheese dressing. It is made simply, and tastes great. Thanks for sharing it.

I think this is really good. I followed it exactly. Next time I would leave out the honey. It’s not bad, just a little different and I like it to be more traditional. I think the other ingredients are perfect and will keep making without the honey or maybe just less. Used it for wings and the consistency was perfect. Could thin out with milk for salad.
Love This! I decreased the mayo some but now I've made it enough times i can just "wing it" pinch of this , pinch of that .Yum!! thanks for the basics.
